subject: Planned controlled restart window in us-east3 — Nov 17 (affects inference workers)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: ops-contacts@acme.com, support@globex.com
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Planned controlled restart window in us-east3 — Nov 17 (affects inference workers)

Hello —

We are scheduling a controlled restart window for the us-east3 inference fleet on Wednesday, Nov 17, 2026 between 00:30–03:30 UTC. This is a staged driver/kernel compatibility refresh intended to improve stability for newer GPU firmware we rolled out last quarter.

What to expect
- Impact: brief rolling restarts of worker processes on a small percentage of nodes (<= 7% at any given time). You may see short-lived 5–15s request retries during a node transition; we are targeting zero request failures and will route traffic automatically to healthy capacity.
- Duration: the tenant-affecting window is 00:30–03:30 UTC; individual requests should not be disrupted for more than a few seconds.
- Scope: inference runtime + driver-level kernel compatibility adjustments; no control-plane changes.

Actions we recommend for Acme teams
1) If you have long-lived streaming sessions, plan to reconnect or checkpoint progress during the window.
2) If you pin model variants tightly, please confirm you have compatible fallback variants configured in the Console (we will automatically fallback to pinned-compatible model IDs when available).

Attachments and links
- maintenance_runbook_v1.2.pdf (attached) — step-by-step runbook and rollback playbook.
- kernel_compat_matrix_v3.csv (attached) — compatibility matrix for common model families.
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-17-maintenance

We will perform a canary in the first 30 minutes and pause for validation. If you prefer we avoid touching your reserved Dedicated pool, reply to this thread and we will exclude it from the rollout.

Apologies for the late notice; this maintenance closes a compatibility gap that has caused two customer-facing evictions in the last 60 days. If you have questions, let us know — we can schedule a short sync.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Ops PM, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planned controlled restart window in us-east3 — Nov 17 (affects inference workers)

Thanks Aisha — please ensure the canary includes a heavy KV-cache workload and a streaming client test (3–5 min) before we proceed to broad rollout. I'll take point on the rollback trigger (any >0.5% error delta over baseline for 2 consecutive minutes triggers pause + rollback).

Also adding Dylan to coordinate alerts and runbook sign-off.

-Markus

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-contacts@acme.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Planned controlled restart window in us-east3 — Nov 17 (affects inference workers)

Hi Aisha — thanks for the heads up. A couple quick questions from our infra team:

1) For clients maintaining long streaming connections, do you preserve KV cache across the short restarts, or is state always invalidated? If invalidated, what is the expected cold-start latency and are there recommendations to warm the cache?
2) We rely on a custom quantized variant that you host — if automatic fallback triggers, will we see increased token latency and is there a way to prefer a cold-startless fallback (e.g., warm a replica beforehand)?

If there's a short call available today to walk through the runbook we'd join.

Thanks,
Maria
Platform Reliability Lead, Acme Corp

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: ops-contacts@acme.com, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planned controlled restart window in us-east3 — Nov 17 (affects inference workers)

Hi Maria — great questions, quick answers below.

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 11:02 AM Markus Klein wrote:
> Thanks Aisha — please ensure the canary includes a heavy KV-cache workload and a streaming client test (3–5 min) before we proceed to broad rollout.

1) KV cache persistence: the controlled restarts are process-level restarts on worker nodes and do not persist in-memory KV cache across the restart. We mitigate by:
   - performing canary sweeps with warmed prefills and validating latency impact before scaling.
   - applying temporary request routing so traffic is routed away from restarting nodes while they rehydrate cache.
   Expected cold-start delta: typically an additional 40–120ms p95 for the first few requests while cache is populated; this falls back to baseline within ~10–30s depending on your sequence lengths and prefill strategies.

2) Fallback behavior for custom quantized variants: automatic fallbacks will prefer model variants tagged as "compatible-fallback" in your deployment config. If you want a warm replica, we can pre-warm one replica in the canary group — please confirm the model ID and we will schedule pre-warming during the canary window. Note that token latency for a fallback to a non-quantized variant may increase by ~5–15% depending on model size.

If you and your infra team can do 20 min today at 17:00 UTC, Markus and I can walk through the runbook and the pre-warm option. Otherwise we can do an on-the-record 10 min check-in tomorrow before the window.

Attachments: maintenance_runbook_v1.2.pdf (see section 2.1 for pre-warm steps)

Thanks —
Aisha

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, ops-contacts@acme.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 20:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-maintenance summary: us-east3 compatibility refresh completed (Nov 17)

Team / Acme —

Summary: the controlled restart window executed overnight on Nov 17 (00:30–03:12 UTC). Canary passed after two validation rounds. We completed staged restarts across the us-east3 pool and validated KV-cache rehydration behavior with the streaming test harness.

Impact observed:
- Brief request retries were observed during node transitions; <0.2% of requests experienced a single retry, no sustained errors or elevated 5xx rates.
- Cold-start delta matched the early estimate (p95 + ~70ms on first requests), recovered within 20–25s on average.
- No customer-facing evictions recorded for pinned Dedicated pools that requested exclusion.

Follow-ups and artifacts:
- Postmortem and runbook updates: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3Cpm-maintenance-runbook
- Incident log and metrics: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-17-maintenance (contains traces and canary graphs)
- We've updated the kernel_compat_matrix_v3.csv to clarify model fallback recommendations (attached).

If you want a short debrief call, happy to schedule. Thanks to Acme for the quick sync and to the infra/ops leads for the seamless canary validation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
